text:
Samir: Heads-up, incoming ticket from AcmePayments: long streaming responses are cutting out mid-run. They see ~4k tokens then connection drops, client reconnects repeatedly and they noticed a spike in billed tokens. Need help reproducing and an interim mitigation.

Tino (Support): Their repro notes: open SSE to /v1/streams?model=gpt-long, send prompt that yields ~12k tokens across ~2+ mins. Client sees data up to ~4k tokens (~35s) then connection silently closes (no HTTP error), client does a reconnect using If-None-Match and restarts stream. They attached client logs showing ECONNRESET and repeated reconnect attempts.

Tino (Support): I pulled our edge logs: connection id c-77b, initial 200, then a flush at ~34s with chunk tokens=4100 then connection closed with "idle_timeout" between edge -> runtime. Runtime traces show model still generating afterwards (tokens being produced), so this is a transport/proxy drop. Snippet:
```
[2024-06-27T15:02:11Z] conn=c-77b stream:start model=gpt-long user=acct-acme
[2024-06-27T15:02:45Z] conn=c-77b stream:flush tokens=4100
[2024-06-27T15:02:45Z] conn=c-77b connection:terminated reason=proxy_idle_timeout
[2024-06-27T15:02:46Z] runtime.token: generated up to 12000 tokens (not flushed)
```

Evan (SRE): Sounds like an intermediate proxy idle timeout (ALB default 60s, some NGiNX/Cloudflare configs lower). TCP keepalives alone won't help if the proxy is looking at HTTP/stream idle. Best practice: application-level heartbeats.

Renee (DevEng): Agreed. Two options: (A) emit SSE comment lines (lines that start with `:`) periodically so proxies see activity; (B) emit light `event: checkpoint` SSE events containing minimal JSON with last_token_index and an opaque checkpoint_id. Comments are cheapest because clients ignore them, but checkpoints let clients resume without re-generating tokens.

Priya (Infra): Inventory of likely culprits: ALBs (60s), old org NGiNX proxies (proxy_read_timeout 30s), Cloudflare default (100s for some plans). We should not rely on customers to change infra. Proposal: flip on server-side keepalive comments for hosted endpoints defaulting to every 15s. Configurable per-customer.

Samir: Customer also reported seeing a 401 briefly mid-stream once during a token refresh race on their side; we confirmed streaming auth happens at handshake. If a mid-stream 401 arrives from our side that's a bug. We need to clarify semantics in docs: handshake auth only; any mid-stream auth error should be surfaced as `event: session-expired` and closed with a final payload.

Tino (Support): Customer asks about billing: they were charged for tokens beyond what the client actually received. How do we determine what to refund?

Evan (SRE): Billing only should count tokens that were flushed to the socket and observed in our egress logs. Our runtime emits `stream:flush` records with token counts and flush offsets. We can reconcile flush records vs billing ingest. If runtime generated tokens after last flush and connection died before flush, those shouldn't be billed. For quick win: manual audit and credit AcmePayments. For long-term: add automated reconciliation that compares runtime flush events with billing entries daily and auto-credit if mismatch exceeds threshold.

Renee (DevEng): Implementation notes for SSE:
```
// server-side pseudo (node)
res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream');
res.write(':welcome\n\n'); // initial comment
const heartbeat = setInterval(() => {
  res.write(':hb ' + Date.now() + "\n\n"); // comment keeps proxies from idling
}, 15000);
// on generation flush:
res.write(`data: {"tokens_flushed": ${flushed}, "offset": ${offset}}\n\n`);
// optional checkpoint event to allow resume
res.write('event: checkpoint\n');
res.write(`data: {"checkpoint_id":"ck_123", "last_token_index": ${offset}}\n\n`);
```
Comments: comments (lines beginning with `:`) are ignored by EventSource clients and do not consume token quota. Checkpoints are emitted as regular events and should be small and not tokenized.

Evan (SRE): Client-side resume pattern suggestion: use Last-Event-ID or a custom `Last-Token-Idx` header on reconnect. Server accepts `Last-Event-ID` or `Resume-Checkpoint` header and will serve the remaining tokens from that checkpoint instead of re-running the whole generation (server-side resume requires runtime support). If resume is not supported, client should do exponential backoff and avoid blind immediate reconnects to prevent double consumption.

Tino (Support): Example quick mitigation message for the customer: apologize, explain probable proxy idle timeout, enable server-side keepalives for hosted customers, request their proxy list, and offer a manual refund while we reconcile. I'll send that and ask for their client stack (browser vs server, any reverse proxies).

Priya (Infra): Action items:
1) Enable server-side SSE comment pings behind a feature flag for hosted API; default 15s interval. Rollout to all hosted tenants in 48h if no regressions.
2) Add `checkpoint` SSE event in spec and implement runtime support to produce checkpoints at safe flush points.
3) Add `event: session-expired` for explicit auth/session closures with machine-readable reason.
4) Start a reconciliation job to compare runtime `stream:flush` logs vs billing lines; auto-create credits when mismatches > 500 tokens or > 0.5% of daily billed tokens per account.

Evan (SRE): I'll own the reconciliation job and the telemetry instrumentation to ensure `stream:flush` emits reliable offsets/sequence ids. ETA: 3 days for initial patch + 1 day manual refund for AcmePayments.

Renee (DevEng): I'll open PR for SSE comments + checkpoint event and a spec doc for clients showing resume flows (Last-Event-ID, Resume-Checkpoint header). Also note in spec that comments should never be counted as billable tokens.

Samir: Billing/Support: please process manual refund once Evan posts the reconcile snapshot. Tino, include the refund offer in the customer comms and schedule a follow-up call.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-20240627-63 created and assigned to Evan.

Tino (Support): Also flagging an edge case: some clients use HTTP libraries that buffer SSE and only expose full events after a newline; recommend our examples include both raw EventSource and server-sent data that respects small-chunk flush semantics.

Renee (DevEng): Good point. Add an example Go client that sets `Transport.DisableKeepAlives=false` and reads chunks manually, plus a JS example using `EventSource` and `fetch` with `ReadableStream`.

Samir: Thanks all. Tino will coordinate the customer message and refund, Renee + Evan will track runtime changes. Follow-up in 72h.

-- end of thread --
